headline: Denmark's Aarhus Heats 1,900 Homes Using Seawater
meta_description: Six seawater heat pumps in Aarhus, Denmark now warm nearly 2,000 homes by drawing bay water and converting it to heat with remarkable efficiency.
summary_short: Aarhus is pioneering a sustainable heating solution: six seawater heat pumps now warm 1,900 homes by drawing bay water and producing up to 3.5 times more heat than energ…
body:
Six seawater heat pumps in Aarhus, Denmark now warm 1,900 homes by drawing renewable energy directly from the bay. The system pumps up to 1.2 million litres of seawater per hour, converting it into heating for thousands of residents.

What makes this approach remarkable is its efficiency: the heat pumps produce up to 3.5 times as much heat as the electricity they consume. This multiplier effect—known as a coefficient of performance—demonstrates why seawater heating is gaining traction across northern Europe's climate-conscious cities.

For residents in Aarhus, the system offers both environmental and practical benefits. Rather than relying solely on fossil fuels or traditional district heating, homes now tap into the thermal energy stored in the surrounding bay. It's an elegant solution that turns a natural resource into reliable warmth through proven technology, quietly decarbonizing an entire neighbourhood.
quick_facts: Six seawater heat pumps operating in Aarhus, Denmark
Heating 1,900 homes with bay water energy
Draws up to 1.2 million litres of seawater hourly
Produces up to 3.5 times more heat than electricity used
